summary: Dashboard drilldown returns wrong trace anchor after org-level impersonation and API-key swap
description: Issue summary: When a user with org-level impersonation (via API key swap) drills down from a dashboard tile into a trace, the returned trace link opens the trace viewer but the trace anchor and tracehook context do not match the original event. Impact: Users see wrong trace context (different span/time) for ~10-15% of drilldowns from saved dashboards across Cartograph Labs org. This breaks incident workflows and increases mean time to debug. Environment: prod (us-east), affected org on enterprise plan using API-key impersonation for automated report generation. Observed since 2026-03-09 after the org started daily scheduled snapshot exports under a new service account. Reproducibility: Intermittent but ~1 in 10 drilldowns reproduce when the dashboard was generated while impersonating a service account that has an API-key rotation policy enabled.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Log into Console as org-admin (Cartograph Labs) and enable impersonation via API-key swap for a service account.
2) Trigger a scheduled dashboard snapshot generation while impersonating the service account (snapshot includes a drilldown-enabled tile with tracehook parameter).
3) From the dashboard, click the drilldown link for a row that contains a tracehook anchor parameter.
4) Observe the trace viewer opens but the linked span/time does not match the original tile's timestamp or span id.
5) Repeat for several rows; failure occurs intermittently and correlates with times when the snapshot was produced immediately after an API-key rotation event.
logs: Example tracehook param seen in dashboard link: tracehook=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...; when opened the trace viewer shows anchor_id=span-0x7f9c instead of expected span-0x1a3b. Console service logs around 2026-03-09T04:12:21Z show: [console-service] INFO drilldown-link-gen user=svc-reporting org=cartograph-labs impersonation=enabled original_token_id=ak-rot-20260309 new_token_id=ak-rot-20260309-2 signed_anchor=sha256:abc123; later when resolving tracehook: [trace-resolver] WARN signature-mismatch expected=sha256:abc123 got=sha256:def456; fallback-resolve produced anchor span-0x7f9c.
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support (Aisha): confirmed reproduction with customer while reproducing scheduled snapshot flow.
SRE (Mateo) pulled console-service logs and trace-resolver logs; correlation shows mismatch between signed anchor digest and resolver input when impersonation header present.

Hypothesis: API-key impersonation flow performs an internal token re-signing/rewriting for downstream URLs. When snapshots are generated during or immediately after a key rotation, the link's tracehook token may be re-signed with the wrong org/service account context, leading the resolver to compute a different digest and resolve to the wrong trace anchor.
Verified repro locally by simulating a key rotation during snapshot generation; reproduced anchor mismatch consistently when rotation event occurred within the 30s window.

Checked related components: console link generator (v1.22.0) uses canonicalize(org, user, original_anchor) before signing; impersonation middleware rewrites org header during swap which overwrites canonicalization input incorrectly.

Related PR found that changed signing behavior for impersonation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1824 — this PR added a shortcut that inadvertently used live impersonated-org for re-sign instead of preserving original context.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported increased debugging time; attaching example dashboard and snapshot URL. Asked for reproduction steps and logs.

Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-11: Confirmed logs show signature mismatch; I can reproduce locally by toggling api-key rotation. Escalating to Console backend owners. Adding related PR that likely introduced regressive behavior.

Jin Park (Console Engineer) 2026-03-12: Reviewed PR 1824; agree this looks like a regression where impersonation path alters canonicalization inputs. Preparing a patch to capture original org/user for signing when generating persisted links. Will run integration test with snapshot generation under rotation.

Cartograph Labs (Customer) 2026-03-12: Thanks for quick triage — business impact is moderate; scheduled executive on-call will use workaround. Please advise ETA for fix and whether we need to re-generate past snapshots.

Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-13: Hotfix deployed to staging (console v1.23.1-preview). Integration test passed for rotation window. Planning canary to prod tomorrow morning UTC. Will follow up with migration plan for existing snapshots.
resolution: Mitigation: Temporary workaround provided to customer — disable automatic API-key rotation for service account used to generate scheduled snapshots and re-generate snapshots after rotation window passes. Fix: Console backend patched to preserve original signing context when generating drilldown links under impersonation. Patch landed in console v1.23.2 and deployed with a gradual canary rollout to prod (started 2026-03-14). Post-deploy migration: background job to re-sign persisted snapshot links for affected orgs queued (job id: JOB-2026-03-14-77). Follow-ups: add unit/integration tests for impersonation+rotation window, add dashboard SLI to detect tracehook signature mismatches, update runbook at linked Confluence page. Customer notified and offered assisted snapshot refresh; waiting on confirmation for migration window.
